newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares slip back despite strong oil price.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares slip back despite strong oil price.

text.p: Norwegian shares fell back on Wednesday hit by a lack of investor confidence and a slump in metals prices. Not even a 70-cent rally in crude prices to post-Gulf War highs could lift the oil-sensitive bourse, brokers said.
"People see little upside at the moment. Every time the market goes up the sellers come out," said one broker. "Investors are being careful, they're looking for firm direction."
The Total share index relinquished almost 0.5 percent to end at 831.69 points. Turnover was a moderate 558 million crowns.

Oil prices rallied to a high at $23.70 for North Sea benchmark Brent Blend on renewed tensions in the Middle East with U.S. defense officials claiming Iraqi forces fired missiles at U.S. fighter jets over norther Iraq.
At the same time the lowest slump in aluminium in two years sent shivers throughout the non-ferrous metals market.
Norsk Hydro, which produces both oil and aluminium, fell 4.50 crowns to close at 299.50 crowns. Metals producer Elkem closed 0.50 crowns off at 95.50 crowns.
